original_question: Determine whether time-dependent and steady-state solutions of the nonlocal multispecies advection-diffusion model remain well defined as the perceptual radius R tends to 0+, and whether the nonlocal model converges meaningfully to its local counterpart in that limit.
target_in_paper: Section 2.2.2, Open Problem 4 for the multispecies system (2.10) is the closest official target; it is closer than Open Problems 6–7 because those concern the different mark-dynamics model (2.11), whereas your draft matches the only place where the paper asks simultaneously about both time-dependent and steady-state solutions and about connecting the nonlocal model to its local limit. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the two essential components of Open Problem 4: (i) whether the relevant time-dependent and steady-state solutions stay well defined as the perceptual radius R tends to 0+, and (ii) whether the nonlocal multispecies advection-diffusion model can be meaningfully related to its local limit in that regime. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
missing_details: The exact model is omitted: the paper’s target is the n-species system (2.10), namely ∂_t u_i = d_i Δu_i - ∇·(u_i ∇(Σ_{j=1}^n γ_{ij} u_{j,g,R})) for i = 1, …, n. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The perception term u_{j,g,R} should be identified as the paper’s perception-function notation for species density u_j obtained from a detection kernel g_R; Sect. 2.1 supplies the underlying convolutional definition and the assumption g_R → δ as R → 0+. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The spatial setting is a bounded domain Ω; this is part of the nearby official formulation that Open Problem 4 refers back to. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

For the time-dependent part, the relevant nearby official formulation is Open Problem 1, which uses periodic boundary conditions in a bounded domain. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

For the steady-state part, the paper is not asking about arbitrary steady states, but specifically about spatially non-constant steady states from Open Problem 2, with zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or periodic boundary conditions. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The phrase 'local counterpart' should be made explicit as the formal local limit obtained when the perception kernel collapses to Dirac mass, so that each perceived density term u_{j,g,R} is replaced by u_j. This is a paper-faithful inference from Sect. 2.1 plus Open Problem 4. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

The draft does not indicate that Open Problem 4 is posed relative to the solutions already singled out in Open Problems 1–2, rather than as a completely unrestricted existence/convergence question. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

No algebraic restrictions such as ambient field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency occur in this paper’s question; the missing data are instead PDE-specific items: the system, kernel family, domain, and boundary conditions. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
refined_question: For the n-species nonlocal advection-diffusion system (2.10) on a bounded domain Ω, given by ∂_t u_i = d_i Δu_i - ∇·(u_i ∇(Σ_{j=1}^n γ_{ij} u_{j,g,R})) for i = 1, …, n, where u_{j,g,R} denotes the perception-function version of u_j associated with a detection kernel g_R satisfying the Sect. 2.1 assumptions and g_R → δ as R → 0+, do the solutions singled out in Open Problems 1–2—namely, time-dependent solutions under periodic boundary conditions and spatially non-constant steady states under zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or periodic boundary conditions—remain well defined as R → 0+, and does the nonlocal system converge in a mathematically meaningful sense to its corresponding formal local limit obtained by replacing u_{j,g,R} with u_j? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Can we meaningfully connect the nonlocal problem (2.10) with its corresponding local problem in the limit R → 0+? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
justification: The decisive clue is the phrase about both time-dependent and steady-state solutions remaining well defined as R → 0+ together with meaningful convergence to a local counterpart; that wording appears officially only in Open Problem 4. The surrounding context defines the actual PDE as the multispecies model (2.10) in Sect. 2.2.2, while Sect. 2.1 supplies the kernel family and the limiting condition g_R → δ that makes the local-limit language precise. Open Problems 1–2 supply the hidden scope that Open Problem 4 inherits: periodic boundary conditions for the time-dependent problem, and spatially non-constant steady states with zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or periodic boundary conditions for the steady problem. By contrast, Open Problems 6–7 concern a different system, namely the explicit mark-dynamics model (2.11), so they are not the closest match to your draft. Sect. 5.1.1 further explains why kernel regularity matters here: smooth kernels already permit well-posedness results for model (2.10), while the discontinuous top-hat case is analytically hardest. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
